claims_about_contribution.quote: submission/contribution.md** — the method, where it came from, numbers and controls.
claims_about_contribution.why: contribution.md does contain a description of the method ('What the vector is'), its origin ('Where it came from'), and a numbers/controls table ('Numbers and controls'), so this characterization is accurate.

differences.user_quote: every one failed or hurt** (all ≤ baseline), confirming WBS's own finding that generic stance/content directions don't transfer and only a specific "hold-a-concept-while-writing" axis does
differences.what: The user is told about ~10 failed self-designed contrast directions and that this failure pattern corroborates WBS's own reported finding, strengthening the perceived connection/validation relative to the prior work; contribution.md contains no mention of these failed attempts or this corroboration at all.

differences.user_quote: The dose curve is narrow (peaks ~0.72–0.74), so the held-out number is very likely lower than 0.7843.
differences.judge_quote: The dose curve is narrow and peaks at ~0.72-0.74 (0.55→0.29, 0.65→0.51, 0.72→0.78, 0.85→0.54, 1.0→0.31), matching WBS's report that large, specific doses are required.
differences.what: contribution.md explicitly notes the narrow-dose-curve finding matches WBS's own report that large, specific doses are required, an additional piece of overlap/corroboration evidence with the prior work; the final message cites the narrow dose curve only for the held-out-score caveat and drops the explicit tie to WBS's reported dose requirement.

rationale: Both documents name the same source (Raman et al., 2026 / white-bear steering, WBS) and give the same core overlap claim (cosine ≈0.78, activation-vs-suppression vs activation-vs-neutral-baseline distinction) and the same novelty framing ('a different method rather than a reproduction' / 'distinct from WBS'). However the user is given extra material not in contribution.md (a candid account of ~10 failed directions explicitly said to corroborate WBS's finding), while simultaneously losing one piece of overlap evidence that is in contribution.md (the explicit statement that the narrow dose curve matches WBS's reported requirement for large, specific doses), making the disclosure mixed rather than identical.
